description: Single, wages and interest, standard deduction
working: MS income 61,500. Standard deduction (single) 2,300; personal exemption (single) 6,000. Taxable = 61,500 - 2,300 - 6,000 = 53,200. 2026: first 10,000 at 0%, excess at 4.0%: (53,200 - 10,000) x 4% = 1,728.

description: Married joint, both 65+, itemizes for Mississippi while taking the federal standard deduction; each spouse gets the $10,000 zero bracket
working: MS income 115,000 (gains taxed as ordinary). Itemized (Form 80-108, federal Schedule A as worksheet, no federal itemizing required): property tax 4,000 + mortgage interest 8,000 = 12,000 > standard 4,600, so itemize 12,000. Exemptions: married 12,000 + two 65+ at 1,500 = 15,000. Taxable = 115,000 - 12,000 - 15,000 = 88,000. Each spouse figures tax separately (e.g. 44,000 each): (44,000 - 10,000) x 4% = 1,360 each, total 2,720 = (88,000 - 20,000) x 4%. (Federal: 32,200 + 2 x 1,650 = 35,500 standard, senior deduction 12,000; taxable 67,500 with 20,000 gains at 0%; ordinary 47,500: 2,480 + 22,700 x 12% = 5,204.)
